title: Monotonicity of bounded execution
statement: Let $W$ be a word width, $P$ a finite program, $c$ a configuration consisting of a program counter and a memory of $W$-bit words indexed by integers, and $r$ a pair consisting of a Boolean verdict and a memory. If executing $P$ from $c$ for $t$ steps returns $r$, then for every $t' ge t$, executing $P$ from the same configuration for $t'$ steps also returns $r$.
hypotheses_covered: A Boolean verdict and memory pair r
Execution for t steps returns r
